slides.headline: Runner? Here's what Pilates adds
slides.sub: Strength and control for the bits running doesn't train much.

slides.title: Running is repetitive loading
slides.body: Every run is thousands of similar steps. Most running niggles come from doing more than your body is ready for, so building strength and capacity alongside your running makes a lot of sense.

slides.title: Single-leg strength and control
slides.body: Running is basically hopping from one leg to the other. Reformer and mat work for hips, glutes and calves helps you control each landing, especially as you tire late in a run.

slides.title: Trunk control, not a rigid core
slides.body: You don't need a rock-hard core to run well. Pilates trains your trunk to stay steady while your arms and legs move, which is exactly what running asks of it. Breathing gets trained too.

slides.title: Fitting it into your week
slides.body: One or two sessions a week is a good starting point. Slot them on easy days or rest days, and avoid a hard session the day before a long run or race.

slides.title: Clinical Pilates, not a class
slides.body: Our Pilates team assesses how you move and your running history, then builds a program you can progress.

slides.headline: Want to run with more strength?
slides.body: Book a clinical Pilates assessment at Hybrid Physiotherapy. Bring your running goals and we'll build a program around your training.

caption:
Running more but not training anything else? Pilates can fill some gaps.

Most running niggles come from doing more than your body is ready for. Building strength and capacity alongside your running helps. Pilates targets single-leg control through the hips, glutes and calves, and trains your trunk to stay steady while your arms and legs move. No rock-hard core needed.

One or two sessions a week is a good starting point. Put them on easy or rest days, and keep hard sessions away from the day before a long run or race.

Our Pilates team starts with an assessment of how you move and your running history. Book online via the link in bio.

story.headline: Pilates for runners
story.body: Single-leg strength, trunk control and one or two sessions a week on easy days. A good complement to your running.
